data.hypothesis: The measured four-output version used 12 input loads for four results per thread. Two outputs reduce the per-thread neighborhood to ten values, but increase loads per result; a 32-by-4 block keeps an 8-row output span and contiguous-x warps while testing whether the smaller per-thread working set and four-warps-per-block geometry offset that extra load work. The y-index helper also preserves the baseline's special stored endpoint row. Correctness and latency remain for controller measurement.

memory_lessons.applicability: A reference for this register-blocking experiment; one measured candidate does not establish which load/reuse balance is best.
memory_lessons.claim: The measured four-output register-blocked candidate passed correctness and averaged 3.3586 microseconds (three samples); the measured baseline also passed and averaged 3.4940 microseconds. These results support testing a contrasting outputs-per-thread configuration, but do not establish its performance mechanism.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Measure the two-output version against the same baseline and four-output result with oracle correctness and full-run latency.

data.notes: This candidate keeps two outputs per thread, uses a 32-by-4 block to cover the same eight y rows per CTA as the measured four-output version, and corrects the endpoint mapping so row my-1 stays distinct. It computes from A with one kernel launch and no additional allocation. Prior measurements are historical references only; this candidate has not been measured.
transformations: Use two consecutive y outputs per thread and retain their ten-row overlapping input neighborhood in registers.
Launch 32-by-4 blocks so each CTA covers eight y outputs while each warp spans contiguous x values.
Match the baseline halo mapping exactly, including leaving row my-1 distinct; guard edge coordinates.
Keep coefficient expressions, A as the input, one kernel launch, and no additional allocation.
